topic: Parts and Mechanics of the Respiratory System
key_concepts: The respiratory system includes the nose/mouth, trachea, bronchi, bronchioles, and alveoli
Nose hairs and mucus help filter the air we breathe.
The trachea has cartilage rings that keep the airway open.
Bronchi and bronchioles branch to carry air throughout the lungs.
Alveoli are tiny air sacs with a large surface area for gas exchange.
Exhaled air contains more carbon dioxide than inhaled air.
Limewater turns cloudy when carbon dioxide is present.
Carbon dioxide is a waste product of cellular respiration.
The diaphragm is a muscle that separates the chest cavity from the abdomen.
During inhalation the diaphragm moves downward and the lungs expand.
During exhalation the diaphragm moves upward and the lungs contract.
Breathing brings oxygen into the body and releases carbon dioxide.
